title: The Extraction of Tashkent
premise: Isandro Marchetti, a former aviation-safety analyst turned whistle-blower living under four identities, recognizes the tail number of a passenger jet whose records vanish mid-flight — a plane he once flagged for the same 'maintenance anomaly' his superiors buried. The aircraft is a decoy: a state contractor plans to destroy it over Tashkent during a summit and blame a systems failure Isandro's own leaked documents could be twisted to explain. Hunted by both the conspirators and the intelligence officer assigned to catch him, he must ally with her — Nadia, who slowly realizes her duty protects the guilty — to expose the plot before the summit convenes. In the end they stop the attack at cost of Isandro's fourth name and any safe life; he surrenders to testify, choosing truth over survival, while Nadia chooses him over the institution that made her.
about_author: P. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade shuttling between European capitals and Central Asia before turning to fiction full-time. Eriksen writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped inside machinery far larger than themselves.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A sleepless night in a Vilnius boarding house establishes his ritual of identity rotation and the insomnia born of the incident three years ago. He sees a news alert about Flight 7Q-2211 losing transponder data mid-air. Emotional beat: dread reawakened.

chapters.title: The Vanishing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He digs into the flight's records and finds them scrubbed in real time — departure logs, maintenance history, even the tail number's registration. Only someone with institutional access could do this. Emotional beat: the past reaching for him.

chapters.title: Tail Number 447-KM
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He recognizes the airframe from his suppressed 2021 report on the 'Tashkent anomaly.' He drafts an email to an old contact, deletes it, then sends it anyway. Emotional beat: guilt converting into resolve.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Nadia Reva's POV. An intelligence officer is briefed that a leak matching Isandro's fingerprints has surfaced around the vanished flight; she is ordered to find him before the summit. She studies his four names and feels an odd respect. Emotional beat: professional curiosity shading into unease.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Isandro meets his old contact, Dara, in Riga; she confirms the contractor Aerostat Group still runs the same falsification pipeline. They are followed out of the café. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Her agency receives pressure from above to close the file fast and pin the vanished flight on the whistle-blower himself. She notices the evidence package was pre-assembled days before the flight. Emotional beat: first crack in loyalty.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Dara is found dead in an apparent burglary; Isandro burns his third name and moves to Almaty under the fourth. He decodes her dead-drop note: the next 'accident' is scheduled for summit week. Emotional beat: grief hardened into purpose.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia interviews Aerostat executives and catches a rehearsed answer about the tail number. Her report recommending deeper inquiry is returned unsigned and unactioned. Emotional beat: the institution refusing its own eyes.

chapters.title: Almaty Rain
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Nadia corners Isandro in a rain-soaked market; instead of arresting him, she listens as he lays out the falsified maintenance chain. She lets him walk, lying in her log. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Incident Was
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Flashback woven through present action: the 2021 near-miss he reported, the burial of his findings, the colleague who died testing the same fault. He explains to Nadia why he can't run anymore. Emotional beat: confession as catharsis.

chapters.title: The Decoy Doctrine
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia discovers the plan: a second aircraft carrying a delegation will be destroyed over Tashkent during the summit, blamed on the documented 'fault' in Isandro's leaks. The vanished flight was a rehearsal. Emotional beat: horror at how clean the design is.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isandro and Nadia formalize an uneasy alliance in a safehouse — she provides access, he provides the technical map of the falsification. Neither fully trusts the other; both admit it aloud. Emotional beat: trust built deliberately, not assumed.

chapters.title: Inside Aerostat
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Using a resurrected credential, Isandro penetrates Aerostat's scheduling system and finds the summit-week manifest: flight AZ-909, the delegation aircraft, tagged with the same anomaly code. Emotional beat: the trap given a date and a face.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia's handler confronts her with evidence she met Isandro; she stalls, but knows she's being watched now. She passes a warning to Isandro through a laundromat dead drop. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Fugitives together, they wait out a manhunt in a mountain dacha outside Almaty. Quiet scene: shared insomnia, shared stories, the first honest tenderness between them. Emotional beat: love arriving without permission.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Countdown structure: they need the original maintenance records from a Tashkent archive, a sympathetic journalist, and a way past summit security lockdowns. Each requirement costs something. Emotional beat: mounting pressure, dwindling options.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Infiltration of the Tashkent civil aviation archive goes wrong; Isandro retrieves the sealed originals but is identified on camera. Nadia covers his escape and is detained. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of commitment.

chapters.title: Turned
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Interrogated by her own agency, Nadia flips the room: she presents the archive originals and forces a senior officer to choose between covering Aerostat and facing treason charges. Some allies defect to her side. Emotional beat: duty realigned with truth.

chapters.title: AZ-909
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. With hours left, Isandro boards as contracted ground-audit staff to physically block the sabotaged component's activation sequence, guided by Nadia over a burner line. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into focus.

chapters.title: Tashkent, Summit Morning
chapters.summary: Climax. Dual POV. Isandro disables the trigger system minutes before departure as security closes in; Nadia broadcasts the falsification dossier to delegates and press simultaneously. The attack dies unseen; the conspiracy begins collapsing publicly. Emotional beat: breathless triumph edged with loss.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro surrenders voluntarily, giving up his last alias to testify under his real name for the first time since the incident. Hearings begin; Aerostat's leadership is indicted. Emotional beat: peace purchased with exposure.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: Resolution. Dual POV. Months later, Isandro — reduced finally to one name — waits outside a courthouse in the rain. Nadia, resigned from the service, walks up beside him. First full night's sleep promised, if not yet achieved. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
